translationRepairs: (His sons Chengqing and Silizhi carried on his line.)
子承慶嗣立 is a heading listing the sons Chengqing and Sili (嗣立 is the name Sili), not "carried on his line"; "Silizhi" is a garbled name.
He had two sons: Chengqing and Silizhi.
He had two sons: Chengqing and Sili.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.

Zhongzong mourned him deeply, summoned his younger brother Silizhi, then prefect of Xiang, to oversee the funeral, and appointed him vice minister of the Huangmen to succeed his brother's office—such was the esteem in which the family was held.

Zhongzong mourned him deeply, summoned his younger brother Sili, then prefect of Xiang, to oversee the funeral, and appointed him vice minister of the Huangmen to succeed his brother's office—such was the esteem in which the family was held.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.

Their mother, Lady Wang, was very strict with Chengqing; whenever he was to be beaten, Silizhi would bare his back and beg to take the punishment in his stead. When she refused, he would beat himself in secret. Once she found out, she grew more lenient with Chengqing. Commentators likened the brothers to Wang Xiang and Wang Lan of Jin.

Their mother, Lady Wang, was very strict with Chengqing; whenever he was to be beaten, Sili would bare his back and beg to take the punishment in his stead. When she refused, he would beat himself in secret. Once she found out, she grew more lenient with Chengqing. Commentators likened the brothers to Wang Xiang and Wang Lan of Jin.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
When Chengqing resigned as Fenige attendant on account of illness, Empress Wu summoned Silizhi and said, "Your father once told me, 'I have two sons, loyal and filial, fit to serve Your Majesty.'
When Chengqing resigned as Fenige attendant on account of illness, Empress Wu summoned Sili and said, "Your father once told me, 'I have two sons, loyal and filial, fit to serve Your Majesty.'
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
At that time schools had fallen into ruin and the law had grown cruel and excessive; Silizhi submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
At that time schools had fallen into ruin and the law had grown cruel and excessive; Sili submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
His son Changyu served as a staff officer in the Ministry of Rites.
His son Changyu served as vice director of the Catering Bureau.
膳部員外郎 is vice director of the Catering Bureau (under the Ministry of Rites).
Moreover, men such as Di Renjie and Yuan Zhong both suffered wrongful entrapment; under interrogation they too had already falsely confessed.
Moreover, men such as Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong both suffered wrongful entrapment; under interrogation they too had already falsely confessed.
元忠 is Wei Yuanzhong; "Yuan Zhong" wrongly splits the given name as a surname.
I humbly consider that Your Majesty is wise, reverent, and discerning, penetrating the workings of spirit and transformation; since the sage kings Xuanyuan and Haohao, none has equaled you.
I humbly consider that Your Majesty is wise, reverent, and discerning, penetrating the workings of spirit and transformation; since the sage kings Xuanyuan and Shaohao, none has equaled you.
軒、昊 are Xuanyuan (the Yellow Emperor) and Shaohao.
Silizhi and Chengqing were both equally renowned for scholarship and character.
Sili and Chengqing were both equally renowned for scholarship and character.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
During the Changshou era, Silizhi succeeded Chengqing as Fenige attendant.
During the Changshou era, Sili succeeded Chengqing as Fenige attendant.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
In the third year of Chang'an, Chengqing took Silizhi's place as Vice Minister of Personnel; soon afterward he also replaced him in managing state affairs.
In the third year of Chang'an, Chengqing took Sili's place as Vice Minister of Personnel; soon afterward he also replaced him in managing state affairs.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
When Chengqing died, Silizhi again succeeded him as Vice Minister of the Chancellery; in all, four offices passed back and forth between them.
When Chengqing died, Sili again succeeded him as Vice Minister of the Chancellery; in all, four offices passed back and forth between them.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
Silizhi had three sons—Fu, Heng, and Ji—all of whom were well known.
Sili had three sons—Fu, Heng, and Ji—all of whom were well known.
嗣立 is romanized Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
In the seventh year of Tianbao, he again served as Governor of Henan and was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
In the seventh year of Tianbao, he again served as Governor of Henan and was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
尚書左丞 is Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, not a Revenue post.

Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong, Heng's cousin by marriage, once secretly recommended Heng as a man of statecraft and asked to surrender his own rank in exchange; Heng was then promoted to Attending Censor Within the Palace.

Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong, the son of Heng's paternal aunt, once secretly recommended Heng as a man of statecraft and asked to surrender his own rank in exchange; Heng was then promoted to Attending Censor Within the Palace.
姑子 means son of a paternal aunt.

Soon he was restored as Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon afterward appointed Vice Minister of the Phoenix Terrace and Chief Minister.

Soon he was restored as Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon afterward appointed Vice Minister of the Phoenix Terrace and Chief Minister.
尚書左丞 is Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
In the twenty-fourth year he died at seventy-two; he was posthumously made Left Director of the Ministry of Revenue and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.
In the twenty-fourth year he died at seventy-two; he was posthumously made Left Chief Minister of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.
尚書左丞相 is Left Chief Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
Su Gui, courtesy name Changrong, was a native of Wugong in Jingzhao and great-grandson of Wei, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue under the Sui.
Su Gui, courtesy name Changrong, was a native of Wugong in Jingzhao and great-grandson of Wei, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.
僕射/丞 of 尚書 belong to the Department of State Affairs; 侍中 is Director of the Chancellery.

At the beginning of the Shenlong era he entered the capital as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; because he was well versed in law and knew many central-administration precedents, he was specially ordered to revise the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.

At the beginning of the Shenlong era he entered the capital as Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; because he was well versed in law and knew many central-administration precedents, he was specially ordered to revise the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.
僕射/丞 of 尚書 belong to the Department of State Affairs; 侍中 is Director of the Chancellery.
Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Wei Yuanzhong submitted: "Su Gui is a man of integrity, and his loyalty and earnestness are as you see — I hope Your Majesty will take note."
Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wei Yuanzhong submitted: "Su Gui is a man of integrity, and his loyalty and earnestness are as you see — I hope Your Majesty will take note."
僕射/丞 of 尚書 belong to the Department of State Affairs; 侍中 is Director of the Chancellery.
In the third year of Jinglong he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xu.

In the third year of Jinglong he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xu.
僕射/丞 of 尚書 belong to the Department of State Affairs; 侍中 is Director of the Chancellery.
Soon he was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
Soon he was additionally made Director of the Chancellery.
僕射/丞 of 尚書 belong to the Department of State Affairs; 侍中 is Director of the Chancellery.

In the fourth year Emperor Zhongzong died; the death was kept secret and no mourning was announced; Empress Wei summoned the chief ministers Wei Anshi, Wei Juyuan, Xiao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wei Wen, Li Jiao, Wei Silizhi, Tang Xiujing, Zhao Yanzhao, Gui, and eighteen others — nineteen in all — into the inner palace for consultation.

In the fourth year Emperor Zhongzong died; the death was kept secret and no mourning was announced; Empress Wei summoned the chief ministers Wei Anshi, Wei Juyuan, Xiao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wei Wen, Li Jiao, Wei Sili, Tang Xiujing, Zhao Yanzhao, Gui, and eighteen others — nineteen in all — into the inner palace for consultation.
韋嗣立 is Wei Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
At first the final edict entrusted Empress Wei to assist the young ruler in managing state affairs and appointed the Prince of Xiang, Grand Marshal of An, to advise and assist in governance.

At first the final edict entrusted Empress Wei to assist the young ruler in managing state affairs and appointed Li Dan, Prince of Xiang of Anguo, as Grand Commandant to advise and assist in governance.
安國相王太尉: 安國 is part of the princely title and 太尉 is Grand Commandant.

That month the Wei faction was defeated; the Prince of Xiang took the throne and issued an edict: "Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, Duke of Xu, Su Gui — from intimate service at court he has improved the pivot of state; his plans have succeeded and his loyal support has been without reserve.

That month the Wei faction was defeated; the Prince of Xiang took the throne and issued an edict: "Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, Duke of Xu, Su Gui — from intimate service at court he has improved the pivot of state; his plans have succeeded and his loyal support has been without reserve.
尚書右僕射 belongs to the Department of State Affairs.
He is appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; the rest of his posts remain as before."
He is appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; the rest of his posts remain as before."
尚書左僕射 belongs to the Department of State Affairs.

restoring honors at the end of life, the same virtue through the ages — the late Left Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, posthumously granted Minister of Works, Area Commander of Jingzhou, Duke of Xu with posthumous title Wenzhen, Gui — walked the upright path and embodied the Way, outwardly firm and inwardly straight, devoted himself in serving the throne, and humbled himself in observing ritual.

restoring honors at the end of life, the same virtue through the ages — the late Left Chief Minister of the Department of State Affairs, Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, posthumously granted Minister of Works, Area Commander of Jingzhou, Duke of Xu with posthumous title Wenzhen, Gui — walked the upright path and embodied the Way, outwardly firm and inwardly straight, devoted himself in serving the throne, and humbled himself in observing ritual.
尚書左丞相 is Left Chief Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
In the seventeenth year he was additionally posthumously granted Minister of Works.
In the seventeenth year he was additionally posthumously granted Minister of Education (Situ).
司徒 is Minister of Education (Situ), not Minister of Works.

In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, made Grand Councilor of the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery, and together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Jing managed state affairs.

In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, made Grand Councilor of the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery, and together with Director of the Chancellery Song Jing managed state affairs.
侍中 is Director of the Chancellery.
Shen was successively appointed Director in the Right Bureau, Attendant Censor, and Prefect of Xuzhou.
Shen was successively appointed Director in the Right Bureau, Supervising Secretary, and Prefect of Xuzhou.
給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Attendant Censor.
Earlier, when Shen was appointed Attendant Censor, Ting was Vice Director of the Secretariat and submitted a memorial declining the appointment given to Shen.
Earlier, when Shen was appointed Supervising Secretary, Ting was Vice Director of the Secretariat and submitted a memorial declining the appointment given to Shen.
給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Attendant Censor.
Silizhi was employed and inherited the enfeoffment without losing his ease and dignity.
Sili was employed and inherited the enfeoffment without losing his ease and dignity.
嗣立 is Wei Sili; "Silizhi" is a garbled rendering.
Xiangxian stood even higher in personal character and was especially renowned for ministerial talent; Quan Ji was famed for saving many lives, and though he stood alone he suffered no calamity.
Xiangxian stood even higher in personal character and was especially renowned for ministerial talent; his saving of many lives was famed, and though he stood alone he suffered no calamity.
全濟有名 means his saving of many was renowned; Quan Ji is not a person.
